spatial_entity.notes: Historical polity identity. Mbanza Kongo point is capital/context navigation only, not a practice polygon.

claim.spatial_precision: Kingdom-level social and political synthesis; changing eligibility and local distribution remain explicit
claim.summary: Specialist scholarship documents slavery and enslavement in the Kingdom of Kongo from the late fifteenth through eighteenth centuries while emphasizing transformation in who could be enslaved. Early distinctions protected many freeborn Kongos while foreign-born captives could be enslaved and sold; later political conflict eroded those distinctions and expanded vulnerability to enslavement.
claim.notes: The claim records transformation of enslavement rules and vulnerability, not a constant prevalence level or uniform practice across the kingdom.

territorial_practice.notes: Positive kingdom-level historical classification with changing status boundaries. Atlantic export/network participation remains analytically separable. No P-level.

source.title: Slavery and Its Transformation in the Kingdom of Kongo: 1491–1800
source.independence_notes: Single specialist synthesis of Kongo documentation; cited primary records are not mechanically counted as independent votes.
source.reliability_limitations: Emphasizes changing legal/social eligibility and political fragmentation; does not provide a uniform spatial prevalence surface.

evidence.evidence_role: specialist classification and historical transformation synthesis
evidence.locator: Abstract and article scope, pp. 1–22: changing distinction between foreign-born captives, freeborn Kongos, and later expanded enslavement vulnerability.

geometry.resolution_method: UNESCO Mbanza Kongo coordinate used as a capital/navigation point only. It is not a Kingdom of Kongo boundary, slave-trade route geometry, or territorial practice extent.

source.title: Mbanza Kongo, Vestiges of the Capital of the former Kingdom of Kongo — geographical data
